description: What exists in Schnabelglück (Phaser + Matter edition) and which design principles were decided. Every entity points at the code that implements it; tests/design.test.js validates this file and cross-checks it against src/.

concepts.description: Anything that acts in the sea world.
The player character, steered with a single hold/release control.
Something the hero can do with hold (dive) and release (fly), or taps while airborne.
A resource or rule that shapes every run (energy, air, cargo, pace).
Something that can hurt Pip or end the run.
Contact ends the run at once.
Contact costs energy (contactDamage) once and gives brief protection; it never takes cargo or air.
A force on Pip and fish (flowAt) without any contact rule.
Solid scenery in Matter: Pip bounces off and loses energy and speed instead of ending the run.
A harmless animal that shares the water with Pip.
An authored combination entry in a stage's encounter list (kinds joined by '-').
Something that pays points, energy or air.
An item Pip catches or touches.
Points for a skilful action or a streak.
Spectacle rolled per run between the regular encounters (rollSetPieces).
An optional reward placed only on calm 'turtle-turtle-gull' waves.
Scenery only; no gameplay effect.
One special moment per run and stage, at a random wave in the middle (rollRare).
A weather element of the storm stage.
One nest of the journey; order is progression and save index.
What a stage is played towards.
Background decor animal or object, scattered differently every run (rollDecor).
A user-interface screen, dialog or overlay outside the canvas world.

relationTypes.description: The encounter kind or pattern is part of the stage's authored encounter list.
Journey order: the first stage unlocks the second.
The stage's one special moment per run.
The set piece is in the stage's pool for this run's roll.
The hero escapes the hazard with this ability.
The first entity is drawn and collides as part of the second.
The first character launches the second.
Doing or meeting the first pays the second.
The stage finishes at this goal.

relations.note: Chase from CHASE.from = 1 on, not part of the encounter list.
It cannot follow Pip out of the water.
Changing depth shakes it off; it follows more slowly.
An active trick turns the gull into a kick bonus.

rules.statement: Every danger is telegraphed before it can hurt: sharks warn before their dash, divers lock their aim before firing, fishermen announce the cast, puffers startle before they puff, terrain is announced, the great white shows only its fin first, gulls and surfers warn on entering.

check.name: sharks track faster later, telegraph a fixed dash, and stop pursuing above water
diver locks aim before firing, reloads, and missed harpoons award only once
fishermen announce a fixed cast, splash once and retrieve their visible net
puffer gives a full second of anticipation and is dangerous only when puffed
every danger is harmless or announced before it can hurt

rules.statement: Each danger first appears alone before it appears in a combination, across the whole journey.

check.name: the journey introduces dangers before combining them and has activity in every encounter
authored stages introduce individual dangers before combinations and finish safely

rules.statement: Shark bites are fatal, but there is always an escape: surfacing or changing depth; shark pairs leave a free band and never more than two sharks overlap.

check.name: sharks, fishermen and divers end the stage while other creatures only drain energy
every shark pair leaves a reachable band after a visible reaction delay
encounter traces do not repeat and never overlap more than two sharks
surfacing shakes off the great white without a bite

rules.statement: The great white chase never happens in the first stage.

check.name: the great white never appears in the bay

rules.statement: Terrain is solid but never ends a run: Pip bounces off and loses energy and speed.

check.name: every stage bounces Pip off its terrain instead of ending the run

rules.statement: Non-fatal contacts cost energy once, protect briefly and never take cargo or air.

check.name: contacts cost energy once, protect briefly, and never take cargo or air

rules.statement: Every fish gives points and energy, even with a full pouch.

check.name: a full pouch keeps earning points and replenishing energy, including golden fish

rules.statement: An air trick needs three quick taps after a breach (four for a double), so fast play rarely triggers one by accident; it pays once.

check.name: air tricks need a breach and complete turns; triple/quadruple presses award once

rules.statement: A surfer turns away when Pip is low on air below him, so the way up stays clear.

check.name: surfers leave a low-air ascent clear; later layers retain a middle corridor and rewards

rules.statement: Calm set pieces (bait ball, current, dolphins) only appear on calm 'turtle-turtle-gull' waves; shows never overlap each other or a calm piece.

check.name: every run rolls its own set pieces, always on safe waves and never overlapping

rules.statement: Dolphins appear only on the reef, so they stay special.

check.name: dolphins are offered only on the reef

rules.statement: Every run holds its stage's one special moment once, at a random wave in the middle.

check.name: special moment once, at a random wave in the middle

rules.statement: Rare surface moments (ducklings, otters) never overlap other surface traffic: they get a wave whose previous, own and next encounter have nothing on the water (two waves ahead where the stage allows), and surface residents step aside while they are on screen.

evidence.contains: // Moments at the surface (ducklings, otters) get waves with nothing else on the water around them.
// A rare moment on the water has the surface to itself.

check.name: rare surface moments get the surface to themselves

rules.statement: Button text is centred in every button style.

check.name: button styles centre their text

rules.statement: The result screen offers one clear next step: 'to the next nest' after a completed nest (with 'this nest again' as a quiet option), otherwise 'try again'. Souvenir photo and beach are small links; a save retry appears only after a failed save.

check.name: the result screen offers only next nest or this nest again as main actions

rules.statement: All UI text exists in German, English and Spanish, including stage names.

check.name: all supported locales provide player-facing dynamic copy and localized stage names
every translation key exists in de, en and es and every referenced key is defined

rules.statement: The journey score accumulates across nests: 'next nest' starts the next stage with the current score and elapsed journey time; 'this nest again' restarts with the score the nest started with; a start from the menu begins at 0.

check.name: one continuous pace rises smoothly, carries across nests and excludes paused/feeding time
next nest carries the journey score and time, a menu start begins at zero

rules.statement: With reduced motion, flashes are disabled: no frenzy screen flash, no lightning flash, no photo flash animation, no hit-stop or shake.

check.name: reduced motion disables flashes and shakes

rules.statement: A bump is comic, not violent: a short wobble, dizzy stars and a puff of foam instead of a harsh red flash.

check.manual: Whether a reaction reads as comic rather than violent is a subjective visual judgement; review on the design-system page and in play.

rules.statement: The game is portrait-only: a short landscape touch screen pauses the round and asks to rotate; resuming stays explicit.

check.manual: Needs a real touch device or emulated coarse pointer in landscape; not covered by the DOM-free node tests.
